evidence.title: Multisite Pragmatic Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial of the CONCERN Early Warning System
evidence.outcome: In-hospital mortality, length of stay, sepsis and ICU transfer with vs without AI early warning system
evidence.effect: Intervention had 35.6% decreased risk of death (aHR 0.644), 11.2% decreased LOS, 7.5% decreased sepsis risk, and 24.9% increased unanticipated ICU transfer (aHR 1.249) versus usual care.
evidence.quote: A hospital-wide EWS based on nursing surveillance patterns decreased in-hospital mortality, sepsis, and LOS when integrated into the care team’s EHR workflow.

evidence.title: AI-enabled conversational agent increases engagement with cognitive-behavioral therapy: A randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Engagement, symptoms, and adverse events for genAI therapy app versus PDF CBT workbooks in randomized trial
evidence.effect: App group had 2.4 times higher usage frequency and 3.8 times longer usage durations; similar overall symptom improvement; no increase in adverse events versus standard care.
evidence.quote: Importantly, the app was safe, with no increase in adverse events compared to standard care.

evidence.title: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial of artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive analytics monitoring for early detection of clinical deterioration
evidence.outcome: Clinical deterioration events and 21-day mortality with vs without AI risk trajectory display
evidence.effect: No change in primary outcome between groups; more event-free hours in display-on group among those with events but not statistically significant; 11% of patients transferred into or out of display beds.
evidence.quote: Predictive analytics monitoring incorporating continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and displays of risk trajectories coupled with an education plan did not improve patient outcomes or reduce deaths.

evidence.title: Long-term Effect of Machine Learning-Triggered Behavioral Nudges on Serious Illness Conversations and End-of-Life Outcomes Among Patients With Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: End-of-life systemic therapy and other end-of-life outcomes versus usual care
evidence.effect: End-of-life systemic therapy: 7.5% [72 of 957 patients] vs 10.4% [24 of 231 patients]; aOR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.11-0.57]; P = .001. Other end-of-life outcomes did not differ.
evidence.quote: Intervention patients were less likely than control patients to receive systemic therapy at the end of life (all decedents: 7.5% [72 of 957 patients] vs 10.4% [24 of 231 patients]; aOR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.11-0.57]; P = .001; high-risk decedents: 7.2% [50 of 696 patients] vs 8.3% [15 of 181 patients]; aOR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.13-1.04]; P = .06) ( Table ).

evidence.title: Assessment of the Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Association Between Time of Day and Colonoscopy Quality
evidence.outcome: ADR improvement with AI-assisted versus unassisted colonoscopy in randomized trials
evidence.effect: AI-assisted colonoscopy raised ADR and eliminated early-late session gap; AI OR 3.81 (2.10-6.91) in late sessions and 1.60 (1.10-2.34) in early sessions.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, the AI systems showed better assistance ability on ADR in late sessions compared with early sessions (odds ratio, 3.81; 95% CI, 2.10-6.91 vs 1.60; 95% CI, 1.10-2.34).

evidence.title: AI Improves Nodule Detection on Chest Radiographs in a Health Screening Population: A Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Detection rate of actionable lung nodules on chest radiographs, AI vs non-AI arm, randomized
evidence.effect: Detection rate 0.59% (31/5238) in AI group vs 0.25% (13/5238) in non-AI group; OR 2.4; 95% CI 1.3, 4.7; P = .008. Malignant nodule detection 0.15% vs 0.0%.
evidence.quote: The trial met the predefined primary outcome, demonstrating an improved detection rate of actionable nodules in the AI group compared with the non-AI group (0.59% [31 of 5238 participants] vs 0.25% [13 of 5238 participants], respectively; odds ratio, 2.4; 95% CI: 1.3, 4.7; P = .008).

evidence.title: Conventional Versus Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation of Chest Radiographs in Patients With Acute Respiratory Symptoms in Emergency Department: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and false-positive rate of chest radiograph interpretation with vs without AI-CAD in a randomized trial
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 67.2% (317/472) vs 66.0% (324/491), OR 1.02 (0.70-1.49), P=0.917; false-positive rate 19.3% vs 18.5%, OR 1.00 (0.79-1.26), P=0.985; no improvement with AI-CAD.
evidence.quote: AI-CAD did not improve the sensitivity and false-positive rate of CR interpretation for diagnosing acute thoracic disease in patients with acute respiratory symptoms who presented to the ED.

evidence.title: Improving bowel preparation for colonoscopy with a smartphone application driven by artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Adequate bowel preparation rate and BBPS score, AI app vs control, in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Adequate preparation 88.54% vs 65.59% (P<0.001); mean BBPS 6.74±1.25 vs 5.97±1.81 (P<0.001); higher compliance with dietary and purgative instructions.
evidence.quote: In the full analysis set (n = 500), adequate preparation is significantly higher in the AI-driven app group (88.54 vs. 65.59%; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Feasibility and impact of a mental health chatbot on postpartum mental health: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Change in depression symptoms (PHQ-9, EPDS) at 6 weeks, chatbot vs usual care, in an RCT
evidence.effect: PHQ-9 mean decrease 1.32 (SD 3.4) chatbot vs 0.13 (SD 3.01) usual care; 6-week EPDS and GAD-7 did not differ between groups and were similar to baseline.
evidence.quote: 6-week mean Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scores did not differ between groups and were similar to baseline.

evidence.title: A Randomized Trial Comparing the Effectiveness of Pre-test Genetic Counseling Using an Artificial Intelligence Automated Chatbot and Traditional In-person Genetic Counseling in Women Newly Diagnosed with Breast Cancer
evidence.outcome: Knowledge score and satisfaction, chatbot vs in-person genetic counselor pre-test counseling in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Median knowledge score 11 (chatbot) vs 12 (counselor), p = 0.09; median satisfaction score 30 vs 30, p = 0.19; no significant differences.
evidence.quote: There was no significant difference in median knowledge score between Chatbot and traditional counseling (11 vs. 12, p = 0.09) or in median patient satisfaction score (30 vs. 30, p = 0.19).

evidence.title: Does Clinical Decision Support Increase Appropriate Medication Prescribing for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction?
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine : JABFM
evidence.outcome: Prescribing for CVD risk factors, CDS intervention vs control clinics
evidence.effect: Hypertension prescribing 34.9% with CDS use vs 34.9% control (P=.998); dyslipidemia 11.3% vs 8.7% control (P=.044); smoking cessation showed similar pattern to dyslipidemia.
evidence.quote: Prescribing for dyslipidemia was significantly higher at intervention encounters where the CDS system was used (11.3% [95% CI, 9.3 to 13.3]) compared with dismissed (7.7% [95% CI, 6.1 to 9.3]; P = .003) and to control encounters (8.7% [95% CI, 7.0 to 10.4]; P = .044); smoking cessation medication showed a similar pattern.

evidence.title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Functional independence, mortality, and hospital length of stay versus standard care
evidence.effect: 90-day functional independence: odds ratio, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.42-4.0. Mortality: 31% pre-AI versus 13% post-AI; P <.001. No difference in hospital length of stay.
evidence.quote: The study team did not observe any differences in IV tPA treatment times, length of stay, rates of functional independence, or safety outcomes apart from mortality, which decreased after the AI intervention.

evidence.title: Autonomous artificial intelligence increases real-world specialist clinic productivity in a cluster-randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Clinic productivity (completed encounters per hour per specialist) with vs without autonomous AI, in cluster-randomized trial
evidence.effect: AI clinic days had 1.59 encounters/hour (95% CI 1.37-1.80) vs control 1.14 (95% CI 1.02-1.25), a 40% higher productivity; primary endpoint met.
evidence.quote: The prespecified primary endpoint is met: AI leads to 40% higher productivity (1.59 encounters/hour, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.37-1.80) than control (1.14 encounters/hour, 95% CI: 1.02-1.25), p < 0.00; the secondary endpoint (productivity in all patients) is also met.

evidence.title: Effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted system on endoscopic diagnosis of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions: a multicentre, tandem, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Miss rate of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions, AI-first vs routine-first
evidence.effect: Per-lesion miss rates 1.7% (2/118) AI-first vs 6.7% (6/90) routine-first (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.08; p=0.079); per-patient 1.9% vs 5.1% (RR 0.37, 0.08-1.71; p=0.40).
evidence.quote: Per-lesion miss rates were 1·7% (2/118; 95% CI 0·0-4·0) in the AI-first group versus 6·7% (6/90; 1·5-11·8) in the routine-first group (risk ratio 0·25, 95% CI 0·06-1·08; p=0·079).

evidence.title: Use of Voice-Based Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Basal Insulin Prescription Management Among Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
evidence.outcome: Time to optimal insulin dose, adherence, glycemic control versus standard of care in randomized trial
evidence.effect: AI group reached optimal dose sooner (median 15 vs >56 days; P=.006), had better adherence (82.9% vs 50.2%) and more glycemic control (81.3% vs 25.0%; P=.005).
evidence.quote: In this randomized clinical trial of a voice-based conversational AI application that provided autonomous basal insulin management for adults with type 2 diabetes, participants in the AI group had significantly improved time to optimal insulin dose, insulin adherence, glycemic control, and diabetes-related emotional distress compared with those in the standard of care group.

evidence.title: Real-time machine learning-assisted sepsis alert enhances the timeliness of antibiotic administration and diagnostic accuracy in emergency department patients with sepsis: a cluster-randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Proportion of sepsis ED patients receiving antibiotics within 1 and 3 hours, comparing ML alert versus usual process
evidence.effect: Antibiotics within 1 h: 68.4% vs 60.1% (P=0.04); within 3 h: 94.5% vs 89.0% (P=0.02); median TTA 46 vs 50 min.
evidence.quote: The proportions of patients who received antibiotics within 1 and 3 h were higher in the intervention group than in the control group (in 1 h; 68.4 vs. 60.1%, respectively; P = 0.04, in 3 h; 94.5 vs. 89.0%, respectively; P = 0.02).

evidence.title: Using Electronic Health Records to Improve HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis Care: A Randomized Trial
evidence.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
evidence.outcome: Initiation of PrEP care within 90 days (discussion, referral, or prescription fill) in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Nonsignificant increase overall (6.0% vs 4.5%, HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.84 to 2.1); HR 2.59 for HIV providers, 0.89 for non-HIV providers (P-interaction <0.001).
evidence.quote: There was a nonsignificant increase in initiation of PrEP care in the intervention arm (6.0% vs 4.5%, HR 1.32, 95% CI: 0.84 to 2.1).

evidence.title: The Efficacy of Real-time Computer-aided Detection of Colonic Neoplasia in Community Practice: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.venue: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with real-time CADe versus traditional colonoscopy in randomized trial
evidence.effect: ADR 42.5% vs 34.4% (P = .005); mean APC 0.89 vs 0.60 (P < .001); ADR benefit attenuated in second half of study (38.7% vs 34.9%; P = .33).
evidence.quote: The ADR for the CADe group was significantly higher than the traditional colonoscopy group (42.5% vs 34.4%; P = .005).

evidence.title: Clinical Decision Support for Hypertension Management in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Change in mean systolic blood pressure at 180 days, CDS vs usual care (silent mode)
evidence.effect: Mean SBP change -14.6 vs -11.7 mm Hg (P = .005). BP control did not differ (50.4% vs 47.1%). Aligned actions 49.9% vs 34.6% (P < .001).
evidence.quote: From the linear mixed model, there was a statistically significant difference in mean SBP change in the intervention group compared with the usual care group (change, -14.6 [95% CI, -13.1 to -16.0] mm Hg vs -11.7 [-10.2 to -13.1] mm Hg; P = .005).

evidence.title: Health Care Cost Reductions with Machine Learning–Directed Evaluations during Radiation Therapy — An Economic Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Study
evidence.outcome: Acute care visits and total medical costs, ML-directed intervention vs standard care
evidence.effect: Acute care visits per course 0.47 standard vs 0.31 intervention (P=0.04); adjusted costs $3110 vs $1494 per course, difference $1616 (95% CI $1450 to $1783; P=0.03).
evidence.quote: The intervention group had fewer acute care visits per course (standard, 0.47; intervention, 0.31; P=0.04).

evidence.title: AI-Generated Draft Replies Integrated Into Health Records and Physicians' Electronic Communication
evidence.outcome: Physician time reading and replying to messages and reply length with vs without GenAI drafts
evidence.effect: GenAI associated with 21.8% increase in read time (95% CI 5.2% to 41.0%; P=.008), -5.9% reply time (P=.33), 17.9% increase in reply length (P<.001).
evidence.quote: The estimated association of GenAI was a 21.8% increase in read time (95% CI, 5.2% to 41.0%; P = .008), a -5.9% change in reply time (95% CI, -16.6% to 6.2%; P = .33), and a 17.9% increase in reply length (95% CI, 10.1% to 26.2%; P < .001).

evidence.title: AI-enabled electrocardiography alert intervention and all-cause mortality: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial
evidence.outcome: All-cause mortality within 90 days
evidence.effect: Mortality was 3.6% in the intervention group versus 4.3% in the control group; HR = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.70-0.99.
evidence.quote: The trial met its primary outcome, finding that implementation of the AI-ECG alert was associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality within 90 days: 3.6% patients in the intervention group died within 90 days, compared to 4.3% in the control group (4.3%) (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.83, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.70-0.99).

evidence.title: Prognostic clinical decision support for pneumonia in the emergency department: A randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Inappropriate ED disposition in randomized trial of prognostic CDS versus usual care
evidence.effect: Inappropriate disposition 3% usual care vs 2% CDS (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.32-2.95); length of stay similar; adverse safety outcomes uncommon in both arms.
evidence.quote: EHR-based prognostic CDS did not improve ED disposition decisions for children with pneumonia.

evidence.title: Outpatient reception via collaboration between nurses and a large language model: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Patient satisfaction with nurse-LLM collaboration vs nurse alone in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Satisfaction 3.91 ± 0.90 vs 3.39 ± 1.15 in nurse group (P < 0.001); repeated Q&R 3.2% vs 14.4%; negative emotions 2.4% vs 7.8%.
evidence.quote: In a single-center randomized controlled trial involving 2,164 participants, the primary endpoint indicated that the nurse-SSPEC collaboration model received higher satisfaction feedback from patients (3.91 ± 0.90 versus 3.39 ± 1.15 in the nurse group, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence guided screening for cardiomyopathies in an obstetric population: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial
evidence.outcome: Identification of LVSD with AI-guided screening versus usual care in randomized trial
evidence.quote: Using the AI-enabled digital stethoscope, the primary study end point was met with detection of 24 out of 587 (4.1%) versus 12 out of 608 (2.0%) patients with LVSD (intervention versus control odds ratio 2.12, 95% CI 1.05-4.27; P = 0.032).
evidence.sample_unit: pregnant and postpartum women completing baseline visit

evidence.title: Managing Postembolization Syndrome Through a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support System: A Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Nurse caring attitude, pain barrier identification, comfort care competence; patient symptom interference with vs without CDSS
evidence.effect: Experimental group showed statistically significant improvements in patient-centered caring attitude, pain management barrier identification, and comfort care competence; patient symptom interference significantly decreased versus before the intervention.
evidence.quote: Notably, the experimental group exhibited statistically significant improvements in patient-centered caring attitude, pain management barrier identification, and comfort care competence after clinical decision support system implementation.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of the Medical Chatbot PROSCA to Inform Patients About Prostate Cancer: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Patient information needs and informedness, chatbot plus standard information versus standard information alone
evidence.effect: Information needs decreased significantly more in the chatbot group than in the control group (p = 0.035). 71.4% agreed the chatbot improved their informedness, and 90.7% would use it again.
evidence.quote: Our RCT results showed significant benefits of the chatbot in reducing patients' information needs and enhancing their understanding of PC.

evidence.title: Automated patient selection and care coaches to increase advance care planning for patients with cancer
evidence.venue: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
evidence.outcome: Prognosis and advance care planning documentation after ML-based patient selection with care coaches, in a stepped-wedge trial
evidence.effect: Prognosis documentation within 14 days 2.9% vs 1.1% (aOR 4.3, P<.001); ACP documentation 7.7% vs 1.8% (aOR 14.2, P<.001).
evidence.quote: The proportion of visits with prognosis documentation within 14 days was higher in the intervention condition than in the control condition: 2.9% vs 1.1% (adjusted odds ratio = 4.3, P < .001).

evidence.title: Proactive care management of AI-identified at-risk patients decreases preventable admissions
evidence.venue: The American journal of managed care
evidence.outcome: Potentially preventable hospital admissions after AI-identified care management, stepped-wedge design
evidence.effect: Potentially preventable HAs dropped 27% (95% CI -44% to -6%); preventable ED visits showed no significant level drop; all HAs -19% (P=.06); all ED visits -15% (P=.06).
evidence.quote: In the pooled analysis of high-risk and highest-risk patients (n = 3007), potentially preventable HAs showed a statistically significant level drop (-27% [95% CI, -44% to -6%]), without any corresponding change in trends.

evidence.title: Randomized Pilot of a Clinical Decision Support Tool to Increase Suicide Screening for at-Risk Primary Care Patients With Opioid Use Disorder
evidence.outcome: CSSRS suicide risk assessment completion within 14 days after visit
evidence.effect: 20.3% intervention vs 17.4% control completed CSSRS; OR=1.22, 95% CI 0.41-3.65, p=0.70; no significant difference; safety event changes not significantly different
evidence.quote: Regarding the primary outcome, only 17.4% of control and 20.3% of intervention patients had a CSSRS completed at a visit in the 14 days after an eligible outpatient visit, with no significant difference between groups ( Table 2 ; OR=1.22, 95% CI=0.41, 3.65).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for individualized treatment of persistent atrial fibrillation: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Freedom from documented AF at 12 months, AI-guided tailored ablation vs PVI-only, plus safety
evidence.effect: Primary endpoint met: 88% tailored vs 70% anatomical (log-rank P<0.0001). No significant difference in freedom from any atrial arrhythmia after one ablation. Safety endpoint did not differ; procedure and ablation times twice as long.
evidence.quote: However, no significant difference between arms was observed for the freedom from any atrial arrhythmia endpoint after one ablation.

evidence.title: Perioperative goal-directed therapy with artificial intelligence to reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and renal failure in patients undergoing lung surgery: A pilot study
evidence.outcome: Intraoperative hypotension, postoperative AKI, MINS versus standard care in RCT
evidence.effect: Hypotension duration was shorter with HPI (0 vs 2.33 min; p=0.01), but AKI did not differ (6.7% vs 4.2%; p=0.72). MINS trend was lower (17.1% vs 31.8%; p=0.07).
evidence.quote: The incidence of postoperative AKI showed no differences between the groups (6.7 % vs.4.2 %; p = 0.72).

evidence.title: Real-time surveillance system for patient deterioration: a pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: In-hospital mortality, length of stay, sepsis, and ICU transfers with versus without the early warning system
evidence.effect: Intervention had 35.6% lower instantaneous risk of death (aHR 0.64), 11.2% shorter length of stay, and 7.5% lower sepsis risk; unanticipated ICU transfer risk rose 24.9% (aHR 1.25).
evidence.quote: A machine learning-based EWS, modeled on nursing surveillance patterns, decreased inpatient deterioration risk with statistical significance.

evidence.title: Effect of a ChatGPT-based digital counseling intervention on anxiety and depression in patients with cancer: A prospective, randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Change in HADS anxiety and depression scores, ChatGPT counseling vs clinician-led education
evidence.effect: ChatGPT group had lower median HADS-Anxiety (6 vs 8; P=0.002) and HADS-Depression (6 vs 9; P<0.001) than controls; ChatGPT use predicted anxiety reduction (OR 18.684).
evidence.quote: At follow-up, the ChatGPT group exhibited significantly lower median HADS-Anxiety (6 [0-17] vs. 8 [1-17]; P = 0.002) and HADS-Depression (6 [0-20] vs. 9 [0-19]; P < 0.001) scores compared to controls.

evidence.title: Coronary Computed Tomographic Angiography to Optimize the Diagnostic Yield of Invasive Angiography for Low-Risk Patients Screened With Artificial Intelligence: Protocol for the CarDIA-AI Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Proportion of normal or nonobstructive CAD diagnosed via ICA, AI triage versus usual care
evidence.effect: Protocol only; no results yet. 252 patients to be randomized 1:1; 81 enrolled as of April 14, 2025; results expected 2026.
evidence.quote: CarDIA-AI is a pragmatic, open-label, superior randomized controlled trial involving 2 Canadian cardiac centers.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis and prognostication in low ejection fraction using electrocardiograms in inpatient department: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Newly diagnosed low EF within 30 days after ECG, AI-ECG alerts versus standard care
evidence.effect: Detection rose 1.5% vs 1.1% (HR 1.50, 95% CI 1.11-2.03, P=0.023); high-risk patients 13.0% vs 8.9% (HR 1.55); echocardiogram use unchanged (17.1% vs 17.3%).
evidence.quote: The intervention significantly increased the detection of newly diagnosed low EF in the overall cohort (1.5% vs. 1.1%, HR 1.50, 95% CI: 1.11-2.03, P = 0.023), with a more pronounced effect among AI-identified high-risk patients (13.0% vs. 8.9%, HR 1.55, 95% CI: 1.08-2.21).

evidence.title: Clinical Decision Support for Septic Shock in the Emergency Department: A Cluster Randomized Trial
evidence.outcome: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour; hypotensive shock; time-to-antibiotic in stepped-wedge cluster RCT of predictive CDS
evidence.effect: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour: 39.0% intervention vs 38.9% control (aOR 1.07 [0.61-1.88]); shock aOR 1.12 (0.53-2.46); antibiotic timeliness aHR 0.85 (0.63-1.16). No difference.
evidence.quote: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour occurred in 39.0% of patients in the intervention arm versus 38.9% of patients in the control arm (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.07 [0.61-1.88]).
evidence.sample_unit: ED encounters meeting inclusion criteria (children with suspected sepsis)

evidence.title: Economic analysis of an AI-enabled ECG alert system: impact on mortality outcomes from a pragmatic randomized trial
evidence.outcome: 90-day all-cause mortality and cost-effectiveness of AI-ECG alerts versus usual care in randomized trial
evidence.effect: 90-day mortality 3.6% intervention vs 4.3% control; overall cost similar ($6204 vs $5803); ICER $59,500 per death averted (95% CI: $-4657 to $385,950).
evidence.quote: Among 15,965 patients, 90-day all-cause mortality was 3.6% in the intervention group versus 4.3% in controls.

evidence.title: An adaptive AI-based virtual reality sports system for adolescents with excess body weight: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Fat mass change in adolescents randomized to AI VR sports vs control
evidence.effect: REVERIE sports reduced fat mass by mean -4.28 kg (95% CI -6.35 to -2.22) relative to control, with no significant difference vs physical sports (-5.06 kg).
evidence.quote: REVERIE sports intervention was effective in reducing primary outcome fat mass (mean -4.28 kg (95% confidence interval (CI) -6.35 to -2.22), relative to control), with no significant difference compared with physical sports (mean -5.06 kg (95% CI -7.13 to -2.98), relative to control).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled ECGs for Atrial Fibrillation Identification and Enhanced Oral Anticoagulant Adoption: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
evidence.outcome: Mortality, ischemic stroke, and bleeding with AI alerts versus usual care
evidence.effect: All-cause death: HR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.50–1.04]; no significant ischemic stroke or cardiovascular death differences. Post hoc gastrointestinal bleeding: 2.5% versus 6.9%; HR, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15–0.85].
evidence.quote: Regarding secondary end points, the intervention group revealed a numerically lower, but not statistically significant, incidence of all‐cause death (HR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.50–1.04]) compared with the control group (Figure 3A ).

evidence.title: An eyecare foundation model for clinical assistance: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Correct diagnostic rate and referral rate with versus without EyeFM copilot in RCT
evidence.effect: Correct diagnostic rate 92.2% vs 75.4% (P<0.001); referral rate 92.2% vs 80.5% (P<0.001); higher patient compliance with self-management (70.1% vs 49.1%) and referral (33.7% vs 20.2%).
evidence.quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
evidence.outcome: Completion of recommended follow-up within 120 days
evidence.effect: CDSS alone: no improvement. Outreach with/without navigation: System A, 38.2 % or 37.2 % vs 23.5 %, p < 0.001; System B, 25.4 % or 23 % vs. 19.7 %, p = 0.044.
evidence.quote: Both models with patient outreach with or without navigation - but not CDSS alone - increased recommended follow-up.

evidence.title: Expanding care coordination in an integrated health system through causal machine learning
evidence.outcome: 30-day readmission in randomized low-risk patients targeted by causal ML score, intervention vs usual care
evidence.effect: 30-day readmissions 7.7% vs 8.2% in intervention vs usual care, not statistically significant; observed-to-expected readmission ratio decline was statistically significant.
evidence.quote: While 30-day readmissions declined in the intervention group (7.7% vs. 8.2%), the difference was not statistically significant.

evidence.title: Implementing an AI-enhanced clinical decision support system for Stenotrophomonas maltophilia: a survey-based randomized controlled trial of antibiotic precision and impact on survival
evidence.outcome: 14-day mortality in AI-CDSS versus standard practice in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Mortality lower in AI-CDSS group (92/800, 11.5%) than control (121/800, 15.1%), p = 0.03.
evidence.quote: Mortality was lower in the AI-CDSS group (92/800, 11.5%) than in the control group (121/800, 15.1%) (p = 0.03).

evidence.title: An AI-Powered Lifestyle Intervention vs Human Coaching in the Diabetes Prevention Program
evidence.outcome: Composite of weight loss, physical activity, and HbA1c outcomes for AI-led vs human-led DPP in a noninferiority RCT
evidence.effect: Primary outcome achieved by 58/183 (31.7%) AI-led vs 59/185 (31.9%) human-led; risk difference -0.2% (1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%), meeting the noninferiority criterion.
evidence.quote: The primary outcome was achieved by 58 of 183 participants (31.7%) in the AI-led DPP group and 59 of 185 (31.9%) in the human-led DPP group (risk difference, -0.2% [1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%]), meeting the criterion for noninferiority.

evidence.title: Detection of undiagnosed liver cirrhosis via AI-enabled electrocardiogram: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized clinical trial
evidence.outcome: New diagnosis of advanced CLD within 180 days, intervention vs usual care in cluster RCT
evidence.effect: Advanced CLD diagnoses 1.0% vs 0.5% overall (OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.22-3.55, P = 0.007); among ECG-ML-positive patients 4.4% vs 1.1% (OR 4.37).
evidence.quote: The intervention significantly increased new diagnoses of advanced CLD in the overall cohort (1.0% versus 0.5% in the control arm; odds ratio (OR) 2.09, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.22-3.55, P = 0.007).

evidence.title: Enhancing patient education in cataract surgery using a conversational artificial intelligence chatbot: pilot randomized controlled trial
evidence.venue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
evidence.outcome: Knowledge gain, anxiety change, and satisfaction, chatbot plus brochure vs brochure alone
evidence.effect: No significant differences in knowledge gain, anxiety change, or satisfaction (P > .05). 17 of 33 (52%) chatbot-group patients did not engage; SUS 83.1 ± 12.1. Only 35 of 64 completed postoperative questionnaires.
evidence.quote: No significant differences were detected in knowledge gain, anxiety change, or satisfaction ( P > .05).

evidence.title: Generative AI-based low-dose digital subtraction angiography for intra-operative radiation dose reduction: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Radiation dose, operation time and complications with generative AI low-dose DSA versus standard protocols in RCT
evidence.effect: AK 151.3 vs 457.4 mGy (P<0.001); DAP 4009.7 vs 12531.6 μGy m2; operation time 34.8 vs 33.1 min; complications 7.5% vs 8.1% (noninferior).
evidence.quote: The GenDSA-V2 group showed substantially reduced radiation exposure, with an air kerma (AK) of 151.3 ± 125.1 mGy compared to 457.4 ± 407.4 mGy in the standard clinical protocols (SCP) group (mean difference = -306.1 mGy, 95% confidence interval (CI) = -342.3 to -269.9, P < 0.001 for superiority) and a dose-area product (DAP) of 4009.7 ± 2767.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup> versus 12531.6 ± 9145.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup> (mean difference = -8521.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup>, 95% CI = -9333.1 to -7710.7, P < 0.001 for superiority).

evidence.title: Increasing engagement with cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) using generative AI: a randomized controlled trial (RCT)
evidence.outcome: Engagement and symptom change (GAD-7, PHQ-9) for genAI CBT app versus digital workbook, plus adverse events
evidence.effect: genAI raised engagement frequency 2.4x and duration 3.8x versus workbooks. Anxiety and depression outcomes were comparable, with no differences in adverse events. No overall symptom benefit.
evidence.quote: Over six weeks, the genAI solution (n = 322) increases engagement frequency (2.4×) and duration (3.8×) compared to digital workbooks (n = 209), with moderate to large effect sizes.
evidence.sample_unit: participants analyzed (322 genAI app, 209 digital workbook control)

evidence.title: A randomized controlled trial of a WeChat-based artificial intelligence agent for postoperative care in orthopedic patients
evidence.outcome: Patient functional outcomes and satisfaction, AI agent vs doctor-led care in RCT
evidence.effect: AI group had significantly better knee function (IKDC), physical health (PCS), and satisfaction at 1 and 3 months (all p<0.05); differences not significant at 6 months (p>0.05).
evidence.quote: At 1 and 3 months, the AI group achieved significantly better outcomes in knee function (IKDC), physical health (PCS), and overall satisfaction (all p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence for Detection of Precancerous Colonic Lesions in a Fecal Immunochemical Blood Test-Based Organized Screening Program in Italy: A Randomized Control Trial
evidence.outcome: Advanced adenoma detection rate, ADR, and adenomas per colonoscopy with CADe versus standard colonoscopy in randomized trial
evidence.effect: AADR comparable (21.3% vs 20.5%, p=0.794); ADR higher with CADe (67.6% vs 59.8%, p=0.012); APC 1.82 vs 1.34 (p<0.001); withdrawal time longer (17.10 vs 16.13 min, p=0.016).
evidence.quote: AADR was comparable between the groups (21.3% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.794).

evidence.title: Triple cardiovascular disease detection with an artificial intelligence-enabled stethoscope (TRICORDER) in the UK: a cluster-randomised controlled implementation trial
evidence.outcome: Incidence of newly coded heart failure diagnosis, AI stethoscope vs routine care, cluster RCT
evidence.effect: ITT analysis found no significant difference in heart failure detection (IRR 0·94 [95% CI 0·86-1·02]); no difference in community or hospital diagnoses (p>0·05). Per-use analysis showed higher detection.
evidence.quote: Intention-to-treat analysis found heart failure detection did not differ between groups (IRR 0·94 [95% CI 0·86-1·02]); with no difference in community-based or hospital-based diagnoses (p>0·05).

evidence.title: Interval cancer, sensitivity, and specificity comparing AI-supported mammography screening with standard double reading without AI in the MASAI study: a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, population-based, screening-accuracy trial
evidence.outcome: Interval cancer rate versus standard screening
evidence.effect: Interval cancer rates were 1·55 versus 1·76 per 1000 participants; proportion ratio 0·88 (95% CI 0·65-1·18; p=0·41), meeting the 20% non-inferiority margin.
evidence.quote: Interval cancer rates were 1·55 (95% CI 1·23-1·92) and 1·76 (1·42-2·15) per 1000 participants in the intervention and control group respectively, a non-inferior proportion ratio of 0·88 (95% CI 0·65-1·18; p=0·41).

evidence.title: A randomized controlled trial of artificial intelligence-based analytics for clinical deterioration
evidence.outcome: Hours free of clinical deterioration events and 21-day mortality with AI risk display versus usual care
evidence.effect: No change in primary outcome between groups; more event-free hours among those with events in display-on group, not statistically significant; predictive analytics with education did not improve patient outcomes.
evidence.quote: Predictive analytics monitoring incorporating continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and displays of risk trajectories coupled with an education plan did not improve patient outcomes.

evidence.title: Design and Architecture of a Generative-AI-Supported, Nonphysician-Delivered Model for GDMT Optimization in HFrEF: The ASSIST-HF Trial
evidence.outcome: GDMT optimization, NT-proBNP levels, and hospitalizations versus standard care
evidence.effect: At 12 weeks, VA-guided care produced superior GDMT optimization across all medication classes, lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, and fewer hospitalizations than standard care. Numerical effect estimates were not reported.
evidence.quote: At 12 weeks, patients in the VA arm had superior GDMT optimization across all medication classes, lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, and fewer hospitalizations.

evidence.title: A fine-tuned large language model chatbot for multi-scenario radiology cancer care: randomized controlled trial on interaction optimization, emotional support, and provider burnout reduction
evidence.outcome: Dialogue quality, provider burnout and image quality with vs without chatbot in randomized sub-trials
evidence.effect: RHP+REC improved factuality in appointment triage (4.12 vs 3.39, P<0.001), satisfaction in pre-exam preparation (3.73 vs 3.19), and burnout exhaustion (1.85 vs 2.40, P<0.01), but underperformed on empathy in radiology clinic services.
evidence.quote: RHP + REC group demonstrated superior dialogue quality in AT (factuality: 4.12 ± 0.86 vs. 3.39 ± 1.21, P < 0.001) and PP (satisfaction: 3.73 ± 0.11 vs. 3.19 ± 0.18, P < 0.001), with reduced burnout (exhaustion: 1.85 ± 0.91 vs. 2.40 ± 1.22, P < 0.01).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Lung Nodule Evaluation on Low-Dose Chest CT in Asymptomatic Individuals: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Interpretation time, nodule detection rates, follow-up recommendations, and lung cancer diagnoses with vs without AI in randomized trial
evidence.effect: No significant difference in interpretation time (187 vs 172 s, p=.23); higher Lung-RADS-positive detection (16.9% vs 10.3%), all-nodule detection (52.9% vs 32.6%), follow-up LDCT recommendations (15.3% vs 7.4%); no lung cancers diagnosed in either group.
evidence.quote: Use of an AI-based nodule evaluation tool integrated into PACS during real-world clinical workflows was not associated with a significant difference in interpretation times.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence assisted colorectal lesion detection in private practices a randomized controlled study
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with AI-assisted vs traditional colonoscopy in randomized trial
evidence.effect: ADR 34.5% with computer-aided colonoscopy vs 32.9% with traditional colonoscopy (p = 0.656); no significant difference between groups.
evidence.quote: The ADR (CAC:34.5% vs TC:32.9%; p = 0.656) was not significantly different between the groups.

evidence.title: Randomized trial of electronic health record implemented AI risk prediction in kidney transplant care
evidence.outcome: conversation frequency about treatment options
evidence.effect: Conversation frequency did not differ between the intervention and control groups (39% vs 40%).
evidence.quote: Conversation frequency did not differ between groups (intervention 14/36 [39%] vs control 16/40 [40%]; chi-square p = 1.00).

evidence.title: AI-WAR: a novel warfarin management software with a bidirectional LSTM dosing model improves time in therapeutic range
evidence.outcome: Anticoagulation quality (TTR, time in target INR) and adverse events, AI-WAR vs conventional management
evidence.effect: Median TTR 48.7% vs 81.3% (P<0.001); time in target INR 36.3% vs 61.9% (P<0.001); elevated INR 12.0% vs 16.8%; adverse events 9.6% vs 19.7% (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Compared with conventional management, AI-WAR significantly improved median TTR (48.7% vs. 81.3%, P < 0.001), increased time in target INR (36.3% vs. 61.9%, P < 0.001), and reduced both elevated INR percentage (12.0% vs. 16.8%) and overall adverse event rate (9.6% vs. 19.7%, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Shared Decision-Making (SDM) in Rhinology: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Change in decisional conflict (DCS) using ChatGPT-4 versus Google for treatment questions
evidence.effect: DCS fell in both arms (ChatGPT -4.3, 95% CI -7.1 to -1.5, p=0.004; Google -2.7, 95% CI -4.3 to -1.1, p=0.002) with no significant difference between groups; MCQ knowledge and treatment preferences unchanged.
evidence.quote: Both groups showed significant reductions in DCS scores with a mean difference of -4.3 in the ChatGPT arm (95% CI: -7.1 to -1.5, p = 0.004) and -2.7 in the Google arm (95% CI: -4.3 to -1.1, p = 0.002), with no significant difference between groups.

evidence.title: CNS-Obsidian: A Neurosurgical Vision-Language Model Built From Scientific Publications
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic helpfulness ratings and correct diagnosis in differential, CNS-Obsidian vs GPT-4o, in randomized deployment trial
evidence.effect: Positive ratings 40.62% vs 57.89% (P = .230); correct diagnosis in differential 59.38% vs 65.79% (P = .626); 70 consultations evaluated
evidence.quote: Both models included correct diagnosis in approximately 60% of cases (59.38% vs 65.79%, P = .626).

evidence.title: Motivational interviewing chatbot improves lifestyle in primary healthcare settings in a pragmatic randomised controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Lifestyle behaviours and committed action at 12 weeks, chatbot plus usual care vs usual care alone
evidence.effect: Modified ITT (n=460): physical activity +576 MET-min/week, fruit/vegetable intake +0.27 portions/day, committed action +0.95 a.u. versus usual care; effects sustained at 9 months; no serious adverse events.
evidence.quote: Modified intention-to-treat analysis (n = 460) showed significant improvements in the intervention group compared to usual care in physical activity (576 MET-min/week), fruit/vegetable intake (0.27 portions/day), and committed action (0.95 a.u.) at 12 weeks.

evidence.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Effectiveness of the ChulaCancer Mobile Chatbot for Supportive Care of Patients With Breast or Colorectal Cancer Receiving Chemotherapy: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Unscheduled hospital visits for chemotherapy toxicity within 12 weeks, chatbot vs usual care
evidence.effect: Unscheduled visits 15% (3/20) chatbot vs 35% (7/20) usual care (P=.24, not significant). Quality-of-life fatigue (P=.02), global health (P=.04) and physical functioning (P=.04) favored chatbot.
evidence.quote: Unscheduled hospital visits occurred in 15% (3/20) of the chatbot group compared to 35% (7/20) of the usual care group (P=.24).

evidence.title: Preliminary Evaluation of a Large Language Model-Powered Chatbot for Osteoporosis Self-Management Education: Formative Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Patient knowledge, nurse time, and adherence with LLM chatbot vs traditional education in randomized trial
evidence.effect: Postintervention knowledge median 80.0 vs 75.0 (P=.01); nurse time median 5.0 vs 23.0 minutes (P<.001); adherence effects mostly nonsignificant (total adherence P=.33)
evidence.quote: The OPBot group showed significantly higher postintervention knowledge scores than the control group (median 80.0, IQR 70.0-89.0 vs median 75.0, IQR 65.5-80.0; P=.01).

evidence.title: Impact of Availability of Computer-Aided Detection Devices on Adenoma Detection During Colonoscopy: A Cluster Randomized Study
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate change after CADe deployment versus control facilities in randomized design
evidence.effect: ADR rose 4.2 percentage points (50.7% to 54.9%) at CADe sites and fell 0.7 points (51.8% to 51.1%) at controls; adjusted OR 1.22 (95% CI 1.15-1.28).
evidence.quote: Using multivariable regression, CADe availability was associated with a significantly increased odds of adenoma detection (odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15 to 1.28), but was not associated with detection of other lesions or changes in withdrawal time.

evidence.title: Medical Record Abstraction for Quality Improvement in Sepsis Care Using Artificial Intelligence: A Cluster Randomized Trial
evidence.outcome: Effect of LLM-based SEP-1 feedback on compliance, 30-day mortality, and ICU admission in a randomized trial
evidence.effect: SEP-1 compliance 82.9% vs 70.1% (absolute +13.0%, OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.15-3.81, P=.02); no significant differences in ICU admissions or 30-day mortality.
evidence.quote: No significant differences existed in intensive care unit admissions or 30-day mortality.
evidence.sample_unit: patients meeting SEP-1 criteria (treated by 66 attending physicians)

evidence.title: Generative AI-enabled clinical decision support system in primary care: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Expert-adjudicated composite of treatment failure within 14 days, LLM-assisted vs control clinical officers
evidence.effect: Treatment failure in 102/4,693 (2.2%) intervention vs 94/4,654 (2.0%) control; adjusted OR 0.77 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.08, P = 0.13); no safety signal identified.
evidence.quote: The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups.

evidence.title: Automated Calls Added to SMS Reminders Reduce Missed Appointments among High-Risk Patients
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: appointment completion rates
evidence.effect: no-show rate was 1.7 percentage points lower and net completions 1.9 percentage points higher
evidence.quote: The no-show rate was 1.7 percentage points lower (down to 9.6% from 11.3%), and the net number of appointment completions was 1.9 percentage points higher (up to 77.8% from 75.9%) in the group of patients who got an IVR call in addition to text message reminders than in the group of patients who got text message reminders alone.

evidence.title: SmartAlert - Implementing Machine Learning-Driven Clinical Decision Support for Inpatient Laboratory Utilization Reduction
evidence.outcome: CBC results within 52 hours of alert display, plus secondary safety outcomes, in randomized pilot
evidence.effect: CBC results within 52 hours 1.54 vs 1.82 (P<0.01), a 15% relative reduction in repetitive testing, without adverse effect on secondary safety outcomes.
evidence.quote: The results show a significant decrease in the number of CBC results within 52 hours of SmartAlert display (1.54 vs. 1.82; P<0.01) without adverse effect on secondary safety outcomes, representing a 15% relative reduction in repetitive testing.

evidence.title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention
evidence.outcome: Self-reported anxiety, depression, stress, angst, craving with ML-alert-triggered PRSS calls vs standard care
evidence.effect: PRSS arm (n=26) had modest but significant decreases in anxiety, stress, depression, angst composite (all p<0.001) and maximum craving (p=0.011) vs SoC (n=37); drug use recurrence not measured.
evidence.quote: Statistically significant reductions were noted in anxiety, depression, stress, angst, and cravings in the PRSS intervention arm relative to the SoC arm, though the extent of the differences was modest, therefore likely tempering the clinical significance.

evidence.title: Using a Machine-Learning Algorithm to Identify Palliative Care Needs in a Primary Care Population: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: time to 0.1% population palliative care consultation
evidence.effect: 60.9 days for the intervention compared with 71.8 days for the control
evidence.quote: For the primary outcome of time to a palliative care consultation, the median (95% credible interval) time to 0.1% of the primary care adult population receiving the consultation was 60.9 (47.8–79.4) days for the intervention, as compared with 71.8 (50.9–103.8) days for the control (posterior probability of a shorter time with the intervention, 0.88; Fig. 2 ).

evidence.title: Physician-Supervised ChatGPT-Assisted Versus Physician-Led Informed Consent for Reducing Preoperative Anxiety: A Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: postintervention anxiety and recovery
evidence.effect: Postintervention anxiety did not differ between groups (mean difference 0.26), but recovery favored the control.
evidence.quote: After adjustment for baseline STAI-1 and STAI-2 scores, postintervention anxiety did not differ between groups (mean difference, 0.26; 95% CI: -1.45 to 1.97), confirming noninferiority.

evidence.title: A bimodal large language model reduces misalignment in patient education: A double-blinded randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Patient satisfaction, suggestion acceptance, proactive disclosure, and 7-day unplanned recontact in a randomized trial against a text-based LLM
evidence.effect: In 555 patients, Dolphin was associated with greater satisfaction (98.6% vs. 93.8%), suggestion acceptance (76.1% vs. 58.9%; p < 0.001), proactive disclosure (44.6% vs. 26.5%; p < 0.001), and fewer 7-day unplanned recontacts (12.9% vs. 22.9%; p = 0.002).
evidence.quote: In 555 patients, Dolphin was associated with greater patient satisfaction (98.6% vs. 93.8%), suggestion acceptance (76.1% vs. 58.9%; p < 0.001), proactive disclosure (44.6% vs. 26.5%; p < 0.001), and fewer 7-day unplanned recontact (12.9% vs. 22.9%; p = 0.002).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (randomized trial); 64,200 utterances from 16,583 cases in the misalignment analysis

evidence.title: Evaluating AI-assisted detection of fetal intracranial malformations in prenatal ultrasound practice: a multicentre, self-crossover, randomised controlled trial in China
evidence.outcome: Sonographer sensitivity and specificity for fetal intracranial malformations with vs without AI assistance in a randomised crossover trial
evidence.effect: Fetal-based sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023). No AI-related adverse events reported.
evidence.quote: In the fetal-based analysis, sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), with specificity meeting the non-inferiority criterion (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

evidence.title: Bayesian Learning to Reduce Cardiac Risk for Locally Advanced NSCLC Patients Based on Personalized Radiotherapy Prescription
evidence.outcome: Post-radiation hs-cTnT elevation, a surrogate for grade ≥2 cardiovascular adverse events
evidence.effect: hs-cTnT elevation occurred in 20.5% with PART versus 31.9% with standard radiation plans; each sequential cohort included 50 patients.
evidence.quote: The incidence of hs-cTnT elevation was lower in cohort 2 (20.5%) than in cohort 1 (31.9%).

evidence.title: An Artificial Intelligence Copilot System Helps Reduce Mortality Rates of Hemodialysis Patients
evidence.outcome: Three-month mortality in hemodialysis patients, AI-assisted intervention versus control, in a pragmatic randomized trial
evidence.effect: HEWIC-assisted care reduced three-month mortality by 38.3% (5,216 intervention vs 4,749 control patients, 58 centers), with a more pronounced effect in primary hospitals.
evidence.quote: Involving 9,965 hemodialysis patients (5,216 intervention and 4,749 control) from 58 dialysis centers, the trial indicates that HEWIC’s high-risk patient identification and treatment recommendation can help reduce the three-month mortality rate of hemodialysis patients by 38.3%, with a more pronounced effect in primary hospitals.

evidence.title: Clinical Impact of a Sepsis Alert System Plus Electronic Sepsis Navigator Using the Epic Sepsis Prediction Model in the Emergency Department
evidence.outcome: Time from emergency department arrival to initial antimicrobial delivery
evidence.effect: Time to antimicrobials: 3.33 h at site A versus 3.22 h at sites B-D (p = 0.437); adjusted improvement versus site A historical was 2.87 h (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Implementation of an electronic sepsis alert system plus navigator using the Epic SPM showed no difference in time to initial antimicrobial delivery between the contemporaneous SPM alert plus sepsis navigator site and the SIRS-based electronic alert sites within the same health care system.

evidence.title: The impact of a point-of-care visual clinical decision support tool on admissions for cellulitis in the University of Maryland medical system
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
evidence.outcome: Hospital admission for cellulitis and antibiotic use with vs without CDS engagement
evidence.effect: CDS engagement associated with reduced admissions (adjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40-0.97, p=0.04) and antibiotic use (adjusted OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.40-0.99); absolute admission reduction 7.1%; engagement 24.1%.
evidence.quote: CDS engagement was associated with decreased admissions for cellulitis and decreased antibiotic use in this study, despite low levels of CDS engagement.

evidence.title: The impact on clinical outcomes after 1 year of implementation of an artificial intelligence solution for the detection of intracranial hemorrhage
evidence.outcome: 30- and 120-day all-cause mortality and discharge mRS before vs after AI triage implementation
evidence.effect: 30-day mortality 27.7% vs 17.5% (p=0.004); 120-day 31.8% vs 21.7% (p=0.017); mRS at discharge 3.2 vs 2.8 (p=0.044) post-AI vs pre-AI.
evidence.quote: The 30- and 120-day all-cause mortality were significantly reduced in the post-AI group when compared to the pre-AI group (27.7% vs 17.5%; p = 0.004 and 31.8% vs 21.7%; p = 0.017, respectively).

evidence.title: A Risk-Prediction Platform for Acute Kidney Injury and 30-Day Readmission After Colorectal Surgery
evidence.outcome: Acute kidney injury and 30-day readmission after colorectal surgery with vs without risk platform
evidence.effect: AKI fell 2.5% (11.3% to 8.8%) and readmissions fell 3.1% (12% to 8.9%) versus a propensity-matched historical cohort; non-randomized, retrospective design.
evidence.quote: Utilization of the risk-based management platform was associated with a 2.5% decrease in the rate of acute kidney injury (11.3% to 8.8%) and 3.1% decrease in rate of readmissions (12% to 8.9%).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (479 risk-based treatment patients matched to 1437 historical controls)

evidence.title: Using artificial intelligence to predict adverse outcomes in emergency department patients with hyperglycemic crises in real time
evidence.outcome: ICU admission and all-cause mortality in AI vs non-AI groups after HIS integration
evidence.effect: No significant differences in ICU admission or all-cause mortality were detected between the non-AI and AI groups.
evidence.quote: No significant differences in ICU admission or all-cause mortality were detected between the non-AI and AI groups.

evidence.title: Impact of real-life use of artificial intelligence as support for human reading in a population-based breast cancer screening program with mammography and tomosynthesis
evidence.outcome: cancer detection rate, recall rate, and PPV
evidence.effect: AI support increased CDR by 3.2/‰, PPV by 4%, and recall rate by 0.7% compared to reading without AI.
evidence.quote: Comparing global results (including DM and DBT) of double reading with vs. without AI support, we observed an increase in CDR, PPV, and RR by 3.2/‰ (5.8 vs. 9; p < 0.001), 4% (10.6 vs. 14.6; p < 0.001), and 0.7% (5.4 vs. 6.1; p < 0.001) respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: women (screening examinations; 11,998 AI-supported and 11,998 matched historical controls)

evidence.title: Impact of a deep learning sepsis prediction model on quality of care and survival
evidence.outcome: In-hospital sepsis mortality and bundle compliance before versus after AI deployment, quasi-experimental
evidence.effect: 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI 0.3%-3.5%); 5.0% absolute increase in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI 2.4%-8.0%); 4% reduction in 72-h SOFA change.
evidence.quote: The deployment of COMPOSER was significantly associated with a 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative decrease) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI, 0.3%-3.5%), a 5.0% absolute increase (10% relative increase) in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI, 2.4%-8.0%), and a 4% (95% CI, 1.1%-7.1%) reduction in 72-h SOFA change after sepsis onset in causal inference analysis.

evidence.title: The intervention of artificial intelligence to improve the weaning outcomes of patients with mechanical ventilation: Practical applications in the medical intensive care unit and the COVID-19 intensive care unit: A retrospective study
evidence.outcome: Mean MV time, ICU LOS, and hospital LOS with vs without AI-assisted weaning in COVID-19 ICU
evidence.effect: With AI (n=88) vs control (n=43): MV time 244.2 vs 426.0 hours (P=.011), ICU LOS 11.0 vs 18.7 days (P=.001), hospital LOS 23.5 vs 40.4 days (P<.001).
evidence.quote: In the second part of the study, the intervention group (with AI, n = 88) exhibited a shorter mean MV time (244.2 hours vs 426.0 hours, P = .011), ICU LOS (11.0 days vs 18.7 days, P = .001), and hospital LOS (23.5 days vs 40.4 days, P < .001) compared to the control group (without AI, n = 43).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (part 1: 1298 pre-AI, 1107 post-AI; part 2: 43 control, 88 AI)

evidence.title: Effectiveness of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Intervention for Detecting Clinical Deterioration
evidence.outcome: Escalations in care: RRT activation, ICU transfer, or cardiopulmonary arrest
evidence.effect: At the EDI score threshold, absolute risk reduction was −10.4 percentage points (95% CI, −20.1 to −0.8 percentage points; P = .03). Inpatient mortality was not significantly reduced.
evidence.quote: The RDD analysis estimated an absolute risk reduction of −10.4 percentage points (95% CI, −20.1 to −0.8 percentage points; P = .03) in the primary outcome for patients at the EDI score threshold.

evidence.title: Integrated image-based deep learning and language models for primary diabetes care
evidence.outcome: Patient adherence to self-management and DR referral, PCP with vs without DeepDR-LLM
evidence.effect: Newly diagnosed patients in PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm showed better self-management (P<0.05); patients with referral DR more likely to adhere to referrals (P<0.01).
evidence.quote: For patients with referral DR, those in the PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm were more likely to adhere to DR referrals (P < 0.01).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (397 unassisted PCP arm; 372 PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm)

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-based automated CT brain interpretation to accelerate treatment for acute stroke in rural India: An interrupted time series study
evidence.outcome: Time to intervention from NCCT imaging before vs after AI deployment in stroke patients
evidence.effect: Median TTI fell from 80 min (IQR 56.8-139.5) at baseline to 58.5 min (IQR 30.3-118.2) after AI deployment (location shift -21.0, 95% CI -38.0 to -7.0).
evidence.quote: Impact analysis in a total of 174 stroke patients (72 in baseline and 102 after deployment) demonstrated a significant reduction of median TTI from 80 minutes (IQR: 56·8-139·5) during baseline to 58·50 (IQR: 30·3-118.2) minutes after AI deployment (Wilcoxon rank sum test-location shift: -21·0, 95% CI: -38·0, -7·0).
evidence.sample_unit: stroke patients (72 baseline, 102 after AI deployment); diagnostic accuracy on 864 NCCT scans

evidence.title: Effectiveness of a novel artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy system for adenoma detection: a prospective, propensity score-matched, non-randomized controlled study in Korea
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with versus without AI-assisted colonoscopy in real-world practice
evidence.effect: ADR 45.1% vs 38.8% (p=0.010); SSLDR 5.7% vs 2.5% (p=0.001); APC 0.78 vs 0.61 (IRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.13-1.42). Non-randomized prospective comparison.
evidence.quote: The ENAD group had a significantly higher ADR (45.1% vs. 38.8%, p=0.010), higher sessile serrated lesion detection rate (SSLDR) (5.7% vs. 2.5%, p=0.001), higher mean number of adenomas per colonoscopy (APC) (0.78±1.17 vs. 0.61±0.99; incidence risk ratio, 1.27; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-1.42), and longer withdrawal time (9.0±3.4 vs. 8.3±3.1, p<0.001) than the SC group.

evidence.title: Applying AI to Safely and Effectively Scale Care to Address Chronic MSK Conditions
evidence.outcome: Pain response, mental health, engagement, satisfaction and adverse events with AI-supported care versus DCP alone
evidence.effect: Pain response 64% vs 63% (p=0.399); anxiety p=0.928; depression p=0.187; adverse events 0.58% vs 0.69% (p=0.231). Outcomes were similar, so AI-supported scaling did not compromise outcomes.
evidence.quote: Similar improvements in pain response were observed, regardless of the group (response rate: 64% vs. 63%; p = 0.399).

evidence.title: Should they stay or should they go? Stroke transfers across a hospital network pre- and post-implementation of an automated image interpretation and communication platform
evidence.venue: Interventional neuroradiology : journal of peritherapeutic neuroradiology, surgical procedures and related neurosciences
evidence.outcome: Rate of transferred stroke patients treated with EVT before vs after AI implementation
evidence.effect: EVT rate among transfers rose from 32.1% pre-AI to 45.7% post-AI (p=0.02); adjusted OR 1.85 (95% CI 1.12-3.06). Non-randomized pre-post design; outcome is a process measure rather than patient outcomes.
evidence.quote: The rate of transfers treated with EVT significantly increased (32.1% pre-AI vs. 45.7% post-AI, p = 0.02).
evidence.sample_unit: patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting to spoke hospitals

evidence.title: Effect of computer aided detection device on the adenoma detection rate and serrated detection rate among trainee fellows
evidence.venue: JGH open : an open access journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
evidence.outcome: Adenoma and serrated detection rates with versus without CADe, before-after comparison
evidence.effect: SDR rose from 8.92% to 14.1% (P=0.037); ADR+SDR 58% vs 55.1% (P=0.46); withdrawal time 17.33 vs 17.35 min (P=0.98).
evidence.quote: CADe resulted in statistically significant improvement in SDR from 8.92% to 14.1% (P = 0.037).

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of a machine learning-based early warning system for patient deterioration
evidence.venue: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne
evidence.outcome: Non-palliative in-hospital death after ML early warning system implementation versus pre-intervention and control units
evidence.effect: GIM deaths 1.6% v. 2.1% (adjusted RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-1.00); subspecialty 1.9% v. 2.1% (RR 0.89, 0.63-1.28); difference-in-differences RR 0.79 (0.50-1.24), CI crossing 1.
evidence.quote: Non-palliative deaths were significantly lower in the intervention period than the pre-intervention period among patients in GIM (1.6% v. 2.1%; adjusted relative risk [RR] 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-1.00) but not in the subspecialty cohorts (1.9% v. 2.1%; adjusted RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63-1.28).

evidence.title: Effect of artificial intelligence implementation to the latest generation 4K colonoscopy
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection, advanced adenoma, polyp detection rates and polyps per patient with vs without CADe
evidence.quote: The MPP rose from 0.85 in the non-AI group to 1.26 in the AI group (P<0.001).

evidence.title: The Adelaide Score: prospective implementation of an artificial intelligence system to improve hospital and cost efficiency
evidence.outcome: Length of stay, readmission, mortality, and discharge destination with versus without AI, pre-post comparison
evidence.effect: Median LOS 3.1 vs 2.9 days (P=0.028); 7-day readmission 7.1% vs 5.0% (p=0.02); no significant difference in mortality or non-home discharge.
evidence.quote: Relative to the control group, use of the Adelaide Score in the intervention group resulted in significantly shorter median length of stay (3.1 versus 2.9 days, P = 0.028) and significantly lower seven-day readmission rate (7.1 versus 5.0%, p = 0.02).

evidence.title: Clinical implementation of AI-based screening for risk for opioid use disorder in hospitalized adults
evidence.outcome: Addiction medicine consultation rate (primary) and 30-day readmissions (secondary), pre vs post AI screener
evidence.effect: Consultations unchanged (1.35% vs 1.51%, P<0.001 for non-inferiority); 30-day readmissions reduced (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.91, P=0.02); US$6,801 per readmission avoided.
evidence.quote: In secondary outcome analysis, the AI screener was associated with a reduction in 30-day readmissions (odds ratio: 0.53, 95% confidence interval: 0.30-0.91, P = 0.02) with an incremental cost of US$6,801 per readmission avoided, demonstrating its potential as a scalable, cost-effective solution for OUD care.

evidence.title: Implementation of a national AI technology program on cardiovascular outcomes and the health system
evidence.outcome: Mortality and downstream cardiac tests with versus without AI FFR-CT after CCTA
evidence.effect: No difference in all-cause mortality (aHR 1.00, 0.93-1.08) or cardiovascular mortality (aHR 0.96); fewer invasive angiograms (aHR 0.93, P<0.001) and noninvasive tests (189 vs 167 per 1,000).
evidence.quote: Implementation of an AI-diagnostic tool as part of a health intervention program was safe and beneficial to the patient pathway and health system with fewer cardiac tests at 2 years.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence for Kidney Stone Spectra Analysis: Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Quality Assurance in the Clinical Laboratory
evidence.outcome: report revision rate
evidence.effect: The report revision rate was nearly 8 times higher during the AI implementation period compared to the control period (RR 7.9, 95% CI 4.1-15.2).
evidence.quote: The report revision rate during the AI implementation period was nearly 8 times higher than that during the control period (relative risk, 7.9; 95% CI, 4.1-15.2).

evidence.title: Implementing an Automated Prediction Model to Improve Prescribing of HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: New PrEP prescriptions and HIV testing at pilot versus matched control clinics
evidence.effect: New PrEP prescriptions were 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%), but the 5.5% increase in HIV tests per 100 patients was not statistically significant.
evidence.quote: Although numbers of PrEP prescriptions remained low, the proportion of all patients with new PrEP prescriptions was 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics compared with matched control clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%).

evidence.title: Impact of an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Enhanced Electronic Health Record System on Quality Measures in Nursing Homes: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
evidence.outcome: Change in CMS nursing home quality measures after EHR+AI implementation versus EHR-only sites
evidence.effect: Greater improvements in 16 of 18 quality measures in EHR+AI sites; major falls -9% (95% CI -17, -1); residents needing help with daily activities -22% (95% CI -29, -15).
evidence.quote: Statistically greater improvements were observed in 16 of 18 quality measures (89%) in EHR+AI sites, with 11 measures (61%) also meeting the parallel trends assumption.

evidence.title: Real-world use of an artificial intelligence-powered clinical decision support tool for ovarian stimulation
evidence.outcome: Starting and total FSH dose and MII oocytes with vs without AI decision support
evidence.effect: MII oocytes 11.17 vs 11.25; starting FSH 397.09 vs 443.84 IU; total FSH 4,181.77 vs 4,654.71 IU; no adverse events introduced by AI.
evidence.quote: Physician use of AI helped significantly reduce the starting and total FSH doses prescribed to patients without adversely affecting MII outcomes, indicating the potential use of AI in lowering in vitro fertilization costs to patients.

evidence.title: AI-based diagnosis of acute aortic syndrome from noncontrast CT
evidence.outcome: Time to correct diagnostic pathway for patients with initial false suspicion, with vs without iAorta
evidence.effect: Prospective comparative study (n = 13,846): iAorta shortened time to correct diagnostic pathway from an average of 219.7 (115-325) min to 61.6 (43-89) min.
evidence.quote: In the prospective comparative study (n = 13,846), iAorta demonstrated the capability to significantly shorten the time to correct diagnostic pathway for patients with initial false suspicion from an average of 219.7 (115-325) min to 61.6 (43-89) min.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy for colorectal lesion detection: a case-control study on diagnostic accuracy and histopathological agreement
evidence.venue: Arquivos brasileiros de cirurgia digestiva : ABCD = Brazilian archives of digestive surgery
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with AI-assisted versus conventional colonoscopy
evidence.effect: ADR was 60% in the AI group versus 50% in controls, not statistically significant (p>0.05); withdrawal time 29 vs 27 min, no significant difference.
evidence.quote: ADR was higher in the AI group (60%) than in the control group (50%), but this difference was not statistically significant (p>0.05).

evidence.title: A machine learning algorithm for the prediction of complications incorporated in electronic medical records improves type 2 diabetes care
evidence.outcome: Change in HbA1c, LDL-C, BMI quality indicators and therapy initiation, test vs control group
evidence.effect: Test group improved more than controls: HbA1c ≤7.0% +9.0% vs +4.5%; LDL-C <70 +27.9% vs +20.7%; BMI <25 +16.5% vs +11.0%; HbA1c >8.0% -18.4% vs -10.1%.
evidence.quote: Compared to controls, test group patients showed significantly greater improvements in HbA1c ≤7.0 % (+9.0 % vs. +4.5 %), LDL-C <70 mg/dL (+27.9 % vs. +20.7 %), and BMI <25 kg/m2 (+16.5 % vs. +11.0 %), with larger reductions in HbA1c >8.0 % (-18.4 % vs. -10.1 %).

evidence.title: Clinical implementation of an AI-based prediction model for decision support for patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery
evidence.outcome: Postoperative complications (CCI>20, any medical complication) with AI-guided personalized pathways vs standard care
evidence.effect: CCI>20 incidence 19.1% vs 28.0%, adjusted OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.42-0.92; P=0.02); any medical complication 23.7% vs 37.3%, OR 0.53 (0.36-0.76; P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Results from the nonrandomized before/after cohort study showed an incidence proportion of the comprehensive complication index >20 of 19.1% in the personalized treatment group versus 28.0% in the standard-of-care group, adjusted odds ratio of 0.63 (95% confidence interval, 0.42-0.92; P = 0.02).

evidence.title: Clinical validation of an AI-based blood testing device for diagnosis and prognosis of acute infection and sepsis
evidence.outcome: Whether AI improves patient outcomes in an interventional study versus standard care
evidence.effect: Study was non-interventional; potential 60-70% reduction in inappropriate antibiotic false positives/negatives was estimated, and benefit remains unproven pending interventional testing.
evidence.quote: Further clinical testing in an interventional setting is needed to prove actionability and clinical benefit of TriVerity.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Colonoscopy: A Tool, Not a Necessity for Experts
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate and polyp detection rate with versus without AI-assisted colonoscopy
evidence.effect: ADR 35% pre-AI vs 31% with AI (p=0.2); PDR 42% vs 38% (p=0.22); adenomas per colonoscopy 0.62 vs 0.51 (p=0.22); withdrawal time shorter with AI (9.34 vs 10.44 min, p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: ADR was 151 (35%) in the pre-AIAC group and 116 (31%) in AIAC group, with no statistical significance (p = 0.2).

evidence.title: Detecting Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis With Artificial Intelligence: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: ATTR-CM testing positivity and new diagnoses versus historical and contemporary controls
evidence.effect: 24/50 (48%) diagnosed; positivity more than 2.8 times historical controls (15.3%); 18% relative increase in new diagnoses vs prior year; patient outcomes not shown to improve.
evidence.quote: The positivity rate was more than 2.8 times higher than historical controls (15.3%; 95% CI, 13.1%-17.9%; P < .001), with an 18% relative increase in new diagnoses vs the prior year.
evidence.sample_unit: patients tested for amyloidosis after AI flag (of 256 eligible)

evidence.title: The implementation of an artificial intelligence-based software for large vessel occlusion stroke improves door-to-puncture time at a comprehensive stroke center
evidence.outcome: Door-to-groin time and proportion receiving thrombectomy within 90 min before vs after AI implementation, plus clinical outcomes
evidence.effect: Thrombectomy within 90 min rose from 26.5% to 68.1% (p<0.001); median DTG fell from 109 to 75 min (p<0.001). No differences in TICI scores, length of stay, or mortality/hospice rates.
evidence.quote: The proportion of patients undergoing thrombectomy within 90 min increased significantly from 26.5% (95% CI 17.9-36.8%) to 68.1% (95% CI 60.0-75.5%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Bayesian Learning to Reduce Cardiac Risk of Patients With Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Based on Personalized Radiation Therapy Prescription
evidence.venue: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
evidence.outcome: Post-radiation hs-cTnT elevation, a surrogate for grade ≥2 cardiovascular adverse events
evidence.effect: hs-cTnT elevation occurred in 20.5% with PART versus 31.9% with standard radiation plans; each sequential cohort included 50 patients. Statistical significance for this comparison was not reported.
evidence.quote: The incidence of hs-cTnT elevation was 20.5% in cohort 2 compared with 31.9% in cohort 1.

evidence.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Improves Transfer Times at Primary Stroke Centers
evidence.outcome: Door-in-door-out time and EVT receipt pre- vs post-AI implementation at primary stroke centers
evidence.effect: Multivariable regression: 106-minute reduction in DIDO (95% CI -165 to -48) post-AI; no difference in likelihood of EVT post-transfer (OR 2.13, 95% CI 0.88-5.13). Pre-post design, not randomized.
evidence.quote: In multivariable linear regression, patients evaluated with automated LVO detection AI software were associated with a 106-minute (95% CI, -165 to -48 minutes) reduction in DIDO time but no difference in likelihood of EVT post-transfer (odd ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 0.88-5.13).

evidence.title: Augmenting Braden Scores With Predictive Modeling to Reduce Hospital-Acquired Pressure Injuries: A Clinical Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: HAPI events per 1000 census days and injury severity distribution on pilot vs control floors
evidence.effect: Significant shift from full-thickness PIs toward deep tissue injuries on pilot floors (OR 0.09; 95% CI 0.01-0.88; P=.03); HAPI census-day odds reduction not significant (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.34-1.39; P=.38).
evidence.quote: A reduction in the odds of census days with HAPI events to those without was also observed but was not significant in the span of the pilot (odds ratio: 0.69; 95% CI, 0.34-1.39; P =.38).

evidence.title: Effectiveness of AI-enhanced colonoscopy: A case-control study using real world evidence in a young screening age population
evidence.venue: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association
evidence.outcome: Adenoma per colonoscopy and adenoma detection rate with CADe versus routine colonoscopy in real-world practice
evidence.effect: Mean APC 0.602 vs 0.293 (rate ratio 1.80 [1.40–2.32]); ADR 30.4% vs 16.8% (adjusted RR 1.68 [1.27–2.22]); no significant difference in withdrawal time.
evidence.quote: The CADe system was found to significantly increase the mean APC (0.602 vs. 0.293; rate ratio 1.80 [1.40–2.32]; P < 0.001) and ADR, 30.4% with CADe versus 16.8% without CADe (adjusted RR 1.68 [1.27–2.22], P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
evidence.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with versus without CADe in real-world colonoscopy, by procedure order
evidence.effect: CADe ADR 49.9% in first 3 procedures vs 39.4% unassisted; later procedures 39.9% vs 40.9%, so the benefit disappeared later in the day.
evidence.quote: CADe assistance significantly improved ADR during early-day colonoscopies, but this benefit disappeared in later-day procedures.

evidence.title: Chatbot Outreach in Value-Based Preventive Care: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: Preventive care-gap closure with chatbot outreach versus phone, email, mail, and multichannel outreach
evidence.effect: Phone outreach achieved higher compliance than chatbot or multichannel outreach across most groups and years; chatbot beat phone only for diabetes care in 2023 (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.48-2.21).
evidence.quote: Phone outreach consistently achieved higher compliance than chatbot or multichannel outreach across most groups and years.

evidence.title: Impact of an artificial intelligence-driven triage system on workflow and transfer efficiency: stratified analysis of 4548 admissions to four thrombectomy hubs receiving transfers from sixty spokes
evidence.venue: Journal of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry
evidence.outcome: Functional status and mortality at discharge, AI-enabled vs non-AI spokes
evidence.effect: Workflow times and EVT utilisation improved with AI-enabled triage (e.g., DIDO adjusted difference -41.6 min), but clinical outcomes at discharge were similar between groups (all Q>0.05).
evidence.quote: Clinical outcomes, including functional status and mortality at discharge, were similar between groups (all Q>0.05).

evidence.title: Implementation of an AI-Based Clinical Decision Support System Predicting In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in General Wards: A Multicenter Staggered-Implementation Study in Secondary Hospitals in Korea
evidence.outcome: Ward in-hospital cardiac arrest and in-hospital mortality after AI-SaMD implementation versus standard care
evidence.effect: IHCA aRR 0.79 (95% CI 0.65-0.96); mortality aRR 0.85 (95% CI 0.79-0.90); shorter hospital and ICU LOS. Neurological outcome, lead-time and full-code death analyses were not significant.
evidence.quote: In secondary hospitals unable to operate an RRS due to fiscal limitations, implementation of an AI-SaMD as an additional informational layer was associated with lower ward IHCA and in-hospital mortality.

evidence.title: Fracture Detection on Bone Radiographs: The Impact of an AI Tool on Orthopaedic Night Shifts
evidence.outcome: Recall rates and missed fractures before vs after AI fracture detection implementation
evidence.effect: Recalls 31/13,813 (0.22%) pre vs 27/14,842 (0.18%) post, p=0.42; fracture-related recalls 0.19% vs 0.17%, p=0.63; management change 0.0006% vs 0.0005%, p=0.551.
evidence.quote: Gleamer BoneView<sup>®</sup> use was linked to a non-significant decrease in missed fractures by orthopaedists working without on-site radiologists.

evidence.title: Implementation outcomes of AI documentation support in routine clinical practice: A non-randomized controlled trial
